note: ADR-0005: outside Windows only / separates components, so a\x5Cb is one component.
ADR-0005: on Windows both / and \x5C separate components; patterns still use /.
The period sits mid-component because the backslash is an ordinary byte here.
The period starts a component, so leading-period protection rejects the candidate.
Issue #483 / ADR-0005: outside Windows, an outer `/` in an extglob program matches only `/`.
Issue #483 / ADR-0005: on Windows, an outer `/` in a positive extglob matches \x5C like a plain pattern separator.
Issue #483 / ADR-0005: outside Windows, an outer `/` before a negated extglob matches only `/`.
Issue #483 / ADR-0005: on Windows, an outer `/` before a negated extglob matches \x5C.
Issue #483 / ADR-0005: once the outer `/` matches \x5C, the negated group still rejects its excluded alternative.

Issue #483 / ADR-0005: an escaped slash in an extglob stays a literal `/` and does not match \x5C on Windows; zlob 1.6.3 normalizes \x5C to `/` in the pattern without collapsing `//` and returns false as well.
